shorts.description:
Advice to younger dudes on finding a “keeper”:

Watch how they handle bad days.

Anyone can be in love when things are easy. But life is hard. You want someone who can handle it. 

It’s easier to find romance than resilience.
shorts.title: Give Her a Try Before You Buy

shorts.description:
How to identify business bottlenecks: 

Look at everything on your calendar. 

Everything you see is what needs to get removed for you to go to the next level.
shorts.title: You're the Bottleneck — Here's the Fix

shorts.description: Building a $1,000,000 Business for a Stranger in 56 Mins
shorts.title: Marry Her Now and Save $740,000 in Taxes

shorts.description:
Most entrepreneurs can’t help themselves…

When business growth slows, they think ‘What’s something new I can sell my audience?’

Rather than, ‘How I do the hard thing and keep growing my main thing?’

New doesn’t compound.

Better questions better answers.
shorts.title: Stop Selling Because It's Hard? It'll Always Be Hard

shorts.description:
If you make your team’s default timeline for projects and tasks “end of day” instead of “end of week” you move seven times faster.

And it starts with you.

Speed is king.
shorts.title: End Every Meeting With This: Who, What, When

shorts.description:
A big influencer made an off handed content about our shorts. He said "you guys are masters." It shocked me because all we do is:
1) Post a lot of sh*t without worrying about duds
2) Do more until it stops working.
3) Then try more stuff til we find something else. 
That's it.
shorts.title: Give Contractors a Rebate to Fund All Your Content

shorts.description:
The fastest path to $10M is often not the fastest path to $100m.

In this way, patience is strategy.
shorts.title: You're Stopping Yourself by Trying to Do It Too Fast

shorts.description:
If you’re brand new to business, and don’t know how to divide your time, consider a 4-4-4 split:

4hrs promotion: let people know about your stuff

4hrs delivery: give them what u promised

4hrs building: figuring out what to do next and how to do it.

Promote. Deliver. Build.
shorts.title: No One Knows You Exist. That's the Issue.

shorts.description:
In my experience, people buy because of how crisply you articulate their problems to them, not, the benefits of your solution.

The goal is for them to feel understood more than to understand your products/services.
shorts.title: Good Writing Is That Someone Understands. Good Copy Is That People Feel Understood.

shorts.description:
In my experience, people buy because of how crisply you articulate their problems to them, not, the benefits of your solution.

The goal is for them to feel understood more than to understand your products/services.
shorts.title: People Believe Nothing You Say and Everything They Say

shorts.description:
Imagine every past customer still paid you today—how big would your business be?

Once I understood this, I understood how to build a big business.

It takes time. And I had to focus on making stuff people keep buying.

This way effort stacks rather than restarting monthly.
shorts.title: How to Make $100K in 4 Days Without Destroying Your Reputation

shorts.description: Business is surprisingly simple but deceptively hard. On a long enough time horizon, the only thing that matters is making a product everyone loves. If you did only that, you'd beat just about everyone.
shorts.title: Your Promotion and Delivery Are the Same Thing

shorts.description:
Imagine you define success as whatever you want.

Then imagine living that.

Understanding that it’s a single player playing a game they define the rules to, against themselves.

Best part: you can change the rules.
shorts.title: There's No Mariachi Band Coming for You

shorts.description:
Entrepreneurs get held back by people in their lives who think entrepreneurs should somehow lead the same life as them but somehow get a different outcome.

Mediocre in. Mediocre out.
shorts.title: You Don't Want Their Life, So Why Listen to Their Opinion?

shorts.description:
The biggest misconception I had when starting a business was that I would somehow “know enough” to be ready. 

You never will. You have to learn how to operate off incomplete information - with conviction. Start. Then adjust as you learn more. That’s it.
shorts.title: Stop Waiting for the Right Time, Wait for the Right Conditions

shorts.description:
Pricing is the single strongest lever on profit in a business.

And yet - 95% of business owners look at what everyone else is charging, take the average, make that their price and never think about it again.

The problem is - the business owners they’re copying are broke too.
shorts.title: The Perfect Price Is the Maximum a Customer Will Spend

shorts.description:
The single greatest change in my life came from doing one thing:

Ignoring people’s advice who didn't have what I wanted.

This includes parents, friends, acquaintances, and random posts I see on my newsfeed.

The world got quieter, and that made decisions a lot easier.
shorts.title: The Day I Wake Up and Realize I'm Wrong, I'll Change

shorts.description:
The most common constraint for business growth isn't access to capital but allocation of attention.

You don't need more money, you need fewer things to focus on.
shorts.title: Only Focus on the Rate Limiter

shorts.description:
Most people never start making money because they can’t even admit that they suck. 

They stay stuck in the delusion that they somehow have an amazing product that no one wants and no one talks about.

If you were the best, you’d be making money.

So. You’re not. Now work.
shorts.title: You Thinking You're Working Is Getting In The Way Of You Actually Working

shorts.description:
A stranger messaged me for encouraging words as his father had passed away the night before.

Here’s what I sent:

Be the man he’d want you to be. 

Instead of focusing on your sadness, focus on helping everyone else through theirs.

Use the proximity of his death to get you to take the actions you were too afraid to take before. Because the window of time where his death affects you will be finite. But the changes you make can be everlasting.

If you live his values, he lives on through you.

And ask yourself a scary question: how can this make me better? Then answer it. 

Realize that the length of time you mourn has nothing to do with how much you loved him. 

You don’t have to be sad to prove to yourself that you loved him.
shorts.title: You Only Have Two Hands and One Brain. Use Them.

shorts.description: You can’t say you want to make the world a better place, then resent younger people for having it easier than you.
shorts.title: Gen Z Doesn't Work Hard? They Just Don't Want to Work Hard for You

shorts.description:
How I remember my customer objectives: 

“The 4Rs”

Retain: keep paying
Review: leave a testimonial/review
Refer: send other people
Resell: buy other stuff

Save for next time you create a customer journey.
shorts.title: Compress 6 Weeks of Work Into 60 Seconds

shorts.description:
You get more out of trying to be every coaches best student than you do out of trying to be their biggest critic.

Because the only way to prove your point of how bad they are at teaching is to sacrifice your long term success to be ‘right about them’

Better to be wrong and win.
shorts.title: How to Get the Most Out of Any Mentor or Coach

shorts.description:
Pricing is the single strongest lever on profit in a business.

And yet - 95% of business owners look at what everyone else is charging, take the average, make that their price and never think about it again.

shorts.title: Pricing Is the Strongest Lever for Making Money in Business

shorts.description:
Ways to add value to whatever you sell:
1) Speed: charge more to deliver faster
2) Risk: charge more for taking on risk (or eliminating it)
3) Ease: charge more for removing friction/effort they'd normally have to do

I'm always cycling thru these when trying to add value.
shorts.title: How to Win When Your Value Is Invisible

shorts.description:
Every person at some point in their lives needs to decide whether they’re more afraid of failing through action or failing through inaction.

You’re gonna fail either way, but only one of them gets you closer to your goal.
shorts.title: The Reason People Buy Is Not Why They Stay

shorts.description:
If you want to get more leads, spend real time and money building something awesome.

Then give it away.

Then ask those people if they want more of what they just got.

The ol drug dealers trick. It’s why people with great products always have an advantage.
shorts.title: Do It for Free to Break Into Bigger Markets

shorts.description:
You get more out of trying to be every coaches best student than you do out of trying to be their biggest critic.

Because the only way to prove your point of how bad they are at teaching is to sacrifice your long term success to be ‘right about them’

Better to be wrong and win.
shorts.title: Pay for the Answers, Then Take the Test

shorts.description:
5 Steps to solving 99% of sales issues:
1) Actually have an offer not just "buy my thing"
2) Have a written script
3) Practice the script daily (don't allow off script sales)
4) Respond to leads immediately
5) Sell to richer customers

Actually do them rather than nod along.
shorts.title: Set Up Fake Doors in Your Office

shorts.description: All businesses eventually realize they’re not in the selling stuff business they’re in the recruiting people business.
shorts.title: Spend $10,000 a Month on Ads and Hire Way More Than One Tech

shorts.description:
I spoke to a business owner last week who gets to 100% of leads within 60 seconds.

Guess what is close rate OF LEADS was…

55%

Today’s reminder to call your leads faster.
shorts.title: You're Leaving $1,200,000 on the Table by Not Calling Leads Fast Enough

shorts.description:
Six years ago I was selling supplements at my gym and I ran out of inventory on a few key products.

I still had about 20 more consults left that day. And - I still needed to make money.

Result: I ended up selling more than I did when I was fully stocked & learned key lesson…
shorts.title: How to Close 90% of Supplement Sales

shorts.description:
Growth hack: word your problems as personal deficiencies.

“My sales people suck” VS 
“I don’t know how to hire train and manage great salespeople.”

If you can improve it, it’s a skill.
If it’s a skill, you can learn it.

But you have to admit you suck before it can get better.
shorts.title: You Suck at Training (Not Hiring)

shorts.description:
If you need more customers, learn:

Outreach
Content
Ads
Affiliates
Referrals

There is no other way.
shorts.title: How to Market a Dental Clinic With Before and Afters

shorts.description: The reason most businesses don’t grow is something big and obvious - it just hurts the founders ego - so they try and solve every problem but the one that matters.
shorts.title: Why Founders Won't Let You Send DMs From Their Account

shorts.description:
There’s a lot of money left on the table by people selling subscriptions instead of bulk.

I’ll buy a year up front in bulk (especially at a discount) instead of a subscription.

But if I’m only offered a subscription, I might not buy at all. 

And that’s the opportunity.
shorts.title: Sell the Renewal at Month 2, Not Month 12

It’s wild how many people I see giving advice on getting to “8 figures” who aren’t doing 8 figures. 

Same people ask what they need to do differently with their content. 

Tell the truth.
shorts.title: You're Selling a Channel You're Not Using

shorts.description:
I feel like I can consolidate all my dating advice into this:

Become worthy of the caliber of partner you want. 

Then, meet as many people as you can to find them. 

Ignore the rest.
shorts.title: Stop Comparing Your Chapter 1 to Someone's Chapter 10

shorts.description:
You don’t decrease churn.

You increase activation and consumption. 

Then churn decreases as a result.

Inputs vs outputs.
shorts.title: How to Get Clients to Stay Past 6 Months

shorts.description:
Building a brand seems complicated. Here’s my layman .02:

1) What you’ve done
2) What you say you’re gonna do that comes true (at a micro and macro level)
3) Other institutions/people you associate with (directly and indirectly)
4) Keeping 1-2-3 aligned with values you hold.
shorts.title: We're Switching From the Attention Economy to the Trust Economy

shorts.description: Entrepreneurship is an unending process of trading your time for increasingly valuable activities. The myth is that you will get to a point where you no longer are needed, but if you continue to grow as your company does, you will become more valuable, not less.
shorts.title: How to Know When to Hire Your First Employee
